subject.title: [Architecture] Enforce strict typings for command payloads in packages/gateway-protocol

question: Should strict payload typing cover only built-in Gateway methods, or should plugin-registered Gateway methods also gain a schema-backed generic registration contract?
rationale: Current core handlers are statically enumerable, but the public plugin API registers method names dynamically; choosing the permanent boundary changes both implementation shape and potential plugin compatibility.

options.title: Stage typed core methods
options.body: Add typed descriptors for built-in methods first and retain the existing generic plugin handler boundary until a separately reviewed plugin API is justified.

options.title: Extend plugin registration
options.body: Design a compatibility-preserving generic registerGatewayMethod contract that accepts payload schemas and derives handler types for both core and plugins.

options.title: Keep runtime-only validation
options.body: Retain generic handler parameters and limit work to narrower assertion helpers where concrete safety problems are demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Stage typed core methods
recommendation.body: Add typed descriptors for built-in methods first and retain the existing generic plugin handler boundary until a separately reviewed plugin API is justified.

likelyOwner.reason: The method descriptor registry and recent Gateway protocol history make this the strongest available owner for the core-versus-plugin contract decision.
